en.headline: Customs seizes 400 suspected poisonous slimming injections from Japan
en.dek: Two local residents were arrested and released on bail after officers found anti-obesity vials valued at about HK$290,000 in a postal packet at the Air Mail Centre.
body: Hong Kong Customs said on Monday it had seized 400 vials of injection suspected to contain Part 1 poisons, with an estimated market value of about HK$290,000, from a postal packet imported from Japan.

Officers inspected the packet at the Air Mail Centre on 5 September and found the anti-obesity injection vials. Follow-up investigation led to the arrest on 8 and 23 September of a 45-year-old local man who collected the parcel and a 41-year-old local woman named as the consignee. Both were released on bail. An investigation continues.

Under the Import and Export Ordinance, importing pharmaceutical products without a valid licence carries a maximum penalty of a HK$500,000 fine and two years’ imprisonment. Possession of Part 1 poisons outside permitted conditions under the Pharmacy and Poisons Ordinance can bring a fine of HK$100,000 and two years’ imprisonment.

zh.headline: 海關檢獲400支疑來自日本有毒減肥針劑 拘兩人
zh.dek: 海關在空郵中心截獲懷疑含第一部毒藥的減肥注射劑，市值約29萬元，兩名本地居民被捕後獲准保釋。
body: 香港海關周一表示，在九月偵破一宗輸入懷疑藥劑製品案，檢獲400支懷疑含第一部毒藥的注射劑，估計市值約29萬元。
關員九月五日在空郵中心檢查一個由日本寄出的郵包時，發現該批減肥注射劑。經調查後，九月八日及二十三日分別拘捕一名45歲本地男子（取件人）及一名41歲本地女子（收件人），兩人已獲准保釋，案件仍在調查。
根據《進出口條例》，未持有效進口許可證而輸入藥劑製品及藥物，一經定罪最高可罰款50萬元及監禁兩年；根據《藥劑業及毒藥條例》，非按規定管有第一部毒藥，最高可罰款10萬元及監禁兩年。
